'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Kankara kidnapping]]
***[[Jihadist]] group [[Boko Haram]] claim responsibility for Friday's mass [[kidnapping]] in [[Kankara]], [[Katsina State|Katsina]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-55295701 (BBC News)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]; [[December 2020 Afghanistan targeted killings]]
**A bombing in [[Kabul]] kills the deputy [[governor]] and his secretary, and wounds their bodyguards. In a later attack in the Ghor Province, a deputy provincial council head was killed while another council member and their driver were wounded when a sticky bomb attached to their vehicle detonated. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-shootings-kabul-bombings-taliban-f6ba14d2d5ff6230d43dc54f1e551526 (Associated Press)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2020–21 South Pacific cyclone season]]
**[[Cyclone Yasa|Tropical Cyclone Yasa]] intensifies into a [[Tropical cyclone scales|category 5 storm]]. It is expected to head towards [[Fiji]] later today. [https://www.fbcnews.com.fj/news/tc-yasa-upgraded-to-category-five/ (FBC News)]
*Two magnitude 4.0 [[earthquake]]s occur in Northern [[California]] at around 6:55–7:00 a.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PST]] and are felt from [[San Jose, California|San Jose]] to as far north as [[San Francisco]]. There are no reported injuries or deaths. [https://www.mercurynews.com/2020/12/15/map-pair-of-earthquakes-rattle-morgan-hill/ (''San Jose Mercury News'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Inter-Agency Task Force for the Management of Emerging Infectious Diseases]] mandates the wearing of a "full" [[face shield]] in addition to wearing a [[Cloth face mask|face mask]] when going outside. Face shields were previously compulsory in enclosed areas, such as [[shopping malls]]. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/filipinos-now-required-wear-full-face-shields-masks-outside-homes-covid-19-pandemic (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record 13 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 600. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/south-koreas-daily-virus-fatalities-hit-record-high/2077194 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
****[[Morocco]] surpasses 400,000 total COVID-19 cases. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-12/15/c_139589427.htm (Xinhua)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
****The northwestern [[Nigeria]]n [[States of Nigeria|state]] of [[Kaduna State|Kaduna]] announces the closure of schools from tomorrow due to an increase of COVID-19 cases. [https://punchng.com/breaking-kaduna-shut-schools-over-covid-19/ (The Punch)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
****[[Ontario]] reports 2,275 cases, a new single-day record. [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/news-pmn/canada-news-pmn/ontario-reports-2275-new-covid-19-cases-today-setting-new-single-day-record (''National Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec]]
****[[Premier of Quebec|Quebec Premier]] [[François Legault]] announces that all non-essential businesses in the [[Quebec|province]] will be closed from December 25 until January 11 in order to reduce the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-quebec-orders-all-non-essential-businesses-to-close-from-dec-25-until/ (''The Globe and Mail'')]
***[[Prime Minister of Canada|Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] announces that the [[Canada|country]] has ordered 168,000 doses of [[Moderna]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-canada-idUSO8N2G800S (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
***[[Turkey]] reports a record 235 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 16,881. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-turkey-toll-int/turkeys-daily-covid-19-deaths-at-record-high-235-ministry-idUSKBN28P2CS (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
**[[Russia–United States relations]]
***[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] congratulates [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] for the first time. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/12/15/russias-president-putin-congratulates-joe-biden-on-election-victory.html (CNBC)]
**[[Mexico–United States relations]]
***[[President of Mexico|Mexican President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] congratulates President-elect Joe Biden for the first time. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/putin-congratulates-biden-election/2020/12/15/bd8c3444-3ea8-11eb-b58b-1623f6267960_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Brazil–United States relations]]
***[[President of Brazil|Brazilian President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] congratulates President-elect Joe Biden for the first time. [https://www.wxxinews.org/post/putin-congratulates-biden-his-victory-over-trump (WXXI)]
*[[Kenya–Somalia relations]], [[Foreign relations of Somaliland]]
**The [[Somalia|Somali]] [[Ministry of Information (Somalia)|Minister of Information]] Osman Abubakar Dubbe announces that the [[Federal Government of Somalia|Government of Somalia]] is recalling its diplomatic staff from [[Kenya]] and is giving Kenyan diplomats seven days to leave Somalia. This comes after [[President of Somaliland|Somaliland President]] [[Muse Bihi Abdi]]'s visit to [[Nairobi]] where he was received by [[President of Kenya|Kenyan President]] [[Uhuru Kenyatta]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/somalia-cuts-diplomatic-ties-with-kenya/a-55942327 (DW)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Japan]]
**The [[Tokyo District Court]] [[sentence (law)|sentence]]s [[serial killer]] [[Takahiro Shiraishi]], dubbed the "[[Twitter]] killer", [[capital punishment|to death]], for [[murder]]ing nine people at his apartment in 2017 and [[dismember]]ing their bodies. Shiraishi, who was found mentally competent, pled guilty and told the court his crimes had a sexual motive. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/12/15/asia/japan-twitter-killer-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)] 
*[[LGBT rights in Hungary]]
**The [[National Assembly (Hungary)|National Assembly]] passes a number of changes to the [[Constitution of Hungary]] which bar same-sex couples from [[LGBT adoption|adopting]] children. The amendments also lowers the legal threshold for the government to declare a [[state of emergency]], and further reduces the oversights the government is required to take with regard to the spending of public funds, which critics say will allow the government to use state money to benefit loyalists. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/15/world/hungary-laws-orban-gay-rights.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Philippine drug war]]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] says that they have found evidence that [[crimes against humanity]] were committed during [[President of the Philippines|Filipino President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]]'s drug war. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2020/12/15/philippines-drug-war-icc-crimes-against-humanity/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Finnish Canadians|Finnish-Canadian]] fashion mogul [[Peter Nygard]] is arrested by [[Law enforcement in Canada|Canadian police]] after being indicted by U.S. authorities on charges of [[sex trafficking]] and racketeering. The U.S. is seeking his [[extradition]] from Canada. Nygard denies the allegations. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-55307723 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Rena Lalgie]] is sworn in as [[Governor of Bermuda]], making it the first time that the [[British Overseas Territories|British territory]] has a black woman as governor. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/bermuda-swears-female-black-governor-74738005 (ABC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2020 United States federal government data breach]]
**[[National Security Advisor (United States)|United States National Security Advisor]] [[Robert C. O'Brien|Robert O'Brien]] interrupts a trip to [[Europe]], returning to [[Washington, D.C.]] to address a cyberattack that is said to have targeted several [[List of federal agencies in the United States|federal government agencies]]. The U.S. [[National Security Council]] announces the formation of a "Cyber Unified Coordination Group," based on [[Presidential Policy Directive 41]]. [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/12/15/obrien-cuts-short-europe-trip-to-address-agency-hacking-445753 (Politico)] [https://www.nextgov.com/cybersecurity/2020/12/what-we-know-about-solarwinds-breach/170792/ (NextGov)]
